description: Chart 11 — The transport network venues sit near. Establishes the supply side before the Melbourne venue-density overlay: train + tram ROUTES (where public transport runs) drawn as lines over the full mesh of ~31,170 PT STOPS (where you can get on), on an equal-area projection of Victoria. This is a proximity/context map, not a service map — lines show where routes go and dots show where stops are, never when or how often services run (GTFS schedule deliberately deferred; the page says 'near', not 'served by'). Full-width and taller than the earlier half-width grid version so Victoria fills the frame and the route skeleton is legible. Colour is held to a neutral slate family so it never competes with the metro/regional teal-orange (the page's reserved emphasis). Data: transport_stops_web.csv as points; pt_routes_simplified.topojson as lines; sa2_summary_simplified.topojson as the base.

layer.description: Base: SA2 boundaries for geographic context (same base as the venue map).

Every public-transport stop in Victoria (all modes), as a faint neutral mesh. Most are bus stops, so the dots read as texture showing how dense the stop network is — the 'where you can get on' layer beneath the rail/tram skeleton.

Train and tram routes as lines — the legible backbone of where public transport runs. Direction/express variants collapsed to one feature per route; bus routes are intentionally not drawn (they would be spaghetti and blow the data budget) and are represented by the stop mesh instead.
